# Unitree G1 loads only articulation configurations and tilts forward, should we modify the model or add control strategy?

> **Current answer:** As per the IsaacLab team, falling when no motion is detected is an expected behavior, and G1_CFG is not an automatic standing controller. A locomotion policy or other closed-loop balance control must be integrated; the team recommends starting from the H1 humanoid policy deployment template. The original thread did not provide a complete strategy for G1, so adaptation and verification remain to be done by the user.

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does the robot tilt forward when only G1 articulation/asset configurations are loaded? Is this a model bug?
- G1 cannot maintain standing in the scenario, and all three Unitree robots in bipeds.py also fall forward.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab's G1_CFG, create_scene.py, and bipeds.py; the original post did not provide precise version numbers for Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim.

- Distinguish between asset/joint configuration definitions that only specify the dynamics model, and whether the scenario actually runs a locomotion or balance policy.

## Possible causes

- The team indicated that falling without motion or balance strategy is an expected behavior.

## Attempts

- The author attempted to reproduce the scenario using the tutorial and bipeds.py; the team recommends integrating the strategy into the H1 humanoid policy deployment template.

## Effective fixes

- Integrate a locomotion policy or other closed-loop balance controller for G1, rather than just loading G1_CFG.

## Result

- The team confirmed this behavior is expected twice, and it is not considered a model bug to be fixed currently.

- When testing standing strategies in real machines, use a harness, limit torque, and emergency stop; do not directly deploy the simulation asset just because it can be loaded in simulation.
